pick.refresh_index.title: Downloads the list of models again (normally cached for 7 days)
pick.hint_download: The corrections are downloaded, only when you choose them, from the AutoEq project (github.com/jaakkopasanen/AutoEq, MIT licence) and saved on the PC: after you choose, the app also works offline.
pick.hint_licence: The measurements behind the corrections belong to their authors (for example oratory1990, Headphone Corner) and have their own terms: some sources, such as oratory1990, forbid commercial use. Rtings measurements are not offered, because their terms forbid reuse. The source of each correction is shown under the preset.
wiz.title: Initial setup
wiz.s0.text: Choose the headphones (or speakers) to apply the equalizer to. Bluetooth headphones must be paired and connected to this PC.
wiz.s1.text: Search for your headphone model: if it is in the AutoEq list, the app downloads the measured correction. You can also skip this step and choose it later.
wiz.s2.with_model: The default preset will be the correction for «{name}». The taste presets (movies, games, music…) are added on top of it.
wiz.s2.no_model: Without a model the Flat preset stays active (no correction): the taste presets still work. You can choose a model later from the Headphones card.
wiz.s2.apo_missing: Equalizer APO is not installed: it is needed to hear the equalization (the instructions appear in the main window).
eq.title: Equalizer
eq.switch.title: Turns the equalization on or bypasses it. In bypass the filters are switched off; with “Uniform volume across presets” the common preamp stays applied, so turning the EQ off does not raise the volume
eq.graphic.hint: The bands add to the selected preset (±12 dB, Q 1.41).
preset.desc.modified: Modified profile: save it as a user preset to keep it.
preamp.bypass_common: Bypass: filters off, the common preamp {common} stays (uniform volume), so the volume does not go up.
preamp.manual: Manual preamp: uniform volume does not change it.
preamp.auto_variable: Automatic preamp for this preset: the volume may change from one preset to another.
preamp.own: Own preamp: this preset needs more attenuation than the common preamp ({common}), to avoid clipping.
preamp.common: Preamp shared by all presets (uniform volume): changing preset does not change the volume.
apply.bypass_common: Bypass on: filters off, the common preamp {preamp} stays.
apply.saved_no_apo: Saved. Install Equalizer APO to hear the equalization.
apo.missing.title: Equalizer APO is not installed.
apo.missing.intro: The equalization is applied by Equalizer APO (free, open source). Steps:
apo.missing.step2: In the Configurator that opens at the end of the installation, select your headphones (“Playback devices” tab) and confirm.
apo.missing.step3: Restart Windows, then reopen this app.
apo.path.included: Config: {path} (the app's file is included from config.txt). If you hear no difference, check in the Equalizer APO Configurator that your headphones are selected.
apo.path.first_save: Config: {path} (the app's file is included from config.txt on first save). If you hear no difference, check in the Equalizer APO Configurator that your headphones are selected.
user.name_required: Type a name for the preset.
user.select_to_delete: Select a user preset to delete.
set.title: Settings
set.autostart.dev: Development build: starting with Windows can only be enabled from the installed version.
set.minimized: Stay hidden in the tray on automatic start
set.default: Set the headphones as default output when they connect
set.uniform.title: All presets use the same preamp, the one of the preset that needs the most. Trade-off: everything sounds a little quieter (raise the volume in the individual apps), but when you change preset, even automatically when a game starts, the volume does not jump and the other apps, for example Discord, stay at the same level. The Windows volume is not touched. “Low-volume listening” keeps its own, lower preamp to avoid clipping; user presets with a manual preamp do not change.
set.uniform.on: Uniform volume on: all presets use the same preamp.
set.uniform.off: Uniform volume off: each preset uses its own preamp.
set.patterns: Bluetooth names to recognise (comma-separated; empty for wired headphones)
set.device: Equalizer APO device (Device: directive, chosen together with the output device)
set.device.applied: Equalizer APO will apply to the devices that contain “{device}”.
auto.title: Automatic presets for apps and games
auto.switch.title: Turns the whole feature on or off
auto.intro: When a game or an app with a rule starts, it switches to the chosen preset; when it closes, the previous preset comes back. If you change preset by hand in the meantime, your choice stays.
auto.status.waiting: Waiting: no game, app with a rule, or movie/music playback detected.
auto.fullscreen: Also treat a full-screen app in the foreground as a game (except browsers and video players)
auto.notify: Windows notification when the preset changes
auto.games_hint: Games detected automatically: executables in the Steam, Epic, GOG, EA, Ubisoft and Xbox libraries, and programs launched from Battle.net, EA app, Ubisoft Connect, GOG Galaxy or the Xbox app.
auto.rules_label: Rules by executable (the first match wins)
auto.rules.empty: No rules. Example: vlc.exe → Film / Cinema.
auto.rule.required: Type the name of an executable, for example vlc.exe.
auto.media.title: Movies and music playing
auto.media.enabled.title: Uses the Windows media session (the one in the volume panel): no periodic polling, the app only wakes up when playback starts, pauses or the track changes
auto.media.hint: Music: YouTube (videos too), YouTube Music, Spotify, Apple Music, TIDAL, Deezer, Amazon Music. Movies: Netflix, Disney+ and Prime Video (apps and browsers), VLC, Windows Media Player and Movies & TV (Music if the file is audio only). In the browser the tab title counts: browser sessions that are not recognised do not change the preset. Priority: game, then movies and music, then the rules by executable. When paused the preset stays for 10 seconds, then the previous one returns.
auto.media.rules_label: Rules by app or site (they win over the built-in ones; the first match wins)
auto.media.rules_hint: The text is searched in the app name (AUMID), in the title and artist being played and in the browser window title.
auto.mrule.required: Type the name of an app or a site, for example twitch.
auto.msg.off: Automatic presets off: if needed, the previous preset comes back.
auto.msg.film_saved: Preset for movies and series saved.
auto.msg.list_refreshed: List of running apps updated: type in the field to see the suggestions.

footer.hint: The window closes to the tray: use “Exit” from the icon menu to quit.

preset.base.name: Correction {title}
preset.base.desc: AutoEq correction of the chosen profile towards the Harman target: brings the headphones' response to the reference target with no other tweaks.
preset.taste.name: {taste} ({base})
preset.flat.name: Flat
preset.flat.desc: No filters: the headphones' original sound.
preset.film.name: Movies / Cinema
preset.film.desc: Deep bass for LFE and explosions, clean low-mids, dialogue up front.
preset.film.why: low shelf 80 Hz +5 dB: the LFE channel reaches 120 Hz [Dolby LFE]; a shelf centred at 80 Hz gives full gain below 40 Hz and almost nothing above 150 Hz; +5 dB is the middle of the 'more bass' preference (4-6 dB) [Olive 2019]. PK 250 Hz -1.5 dB Q 1: removes the low-mid energy that masks the voice [upward spread of masking, Moore]. PK 2 kHz +2 dB Q 0.7 (1-4 kHz): the 1-4 kHz octaves carry 72% of intelligibility [ANSI S3.5 SII]. The cinema X-curve (SMPTE ST 202) is NOT applied: it is meant for large rooms, not headphones.
preset.night.name: TV series / Night dialogue
preset.night.desc: Voice up front and less bass, for low volumes in the evening. An EQ does not compress dynamics: for that, also enable the night mode of your player or TV.
preset.night.why: low shelf 105 Hz -3 dB: reduced Harman bass, as preferred by 21% of listeners (2-3 dB) [Olive 2019], and less low-frequency energy that makes effects and music louder than the voice. PK 2 kHz +3 dB Q 0.7: 1-4 kHz band, 72% of intelligibility [ANSI S3.5 SII].
preset.gaming_fps.name: Competitive gaming / FPS
preset.gaming_fps.desc: Footsteps and positional detail (2-6 kHz) emphasised, bass reduced so explosions do not cover the rest.
preset.gaming_fps.why: low shelf 105 Hz -4 dB: removes 2/3 of the Harman target's bass boost (+6 dB) [Harman]; loud low sounds mask higher ones [upward spread of masking, Moore]. PK 3.5 kHz +3 dB Q 0.9 (about 2-6 kHz): footstep detail and transients, the region where interaural level differences and pinna cues matter for localising sounds.
preset.gaming.name: Immersive gaming
preset.gaming.desc: More bass for explosions and soundtracks, a touch of air at the top for ambience. It is not HRTF spatialisation.
preset.gaming.why: low shelf 105 Hz +4 dB: 'more bass' preference (4-6 dB) [Olive 2019]. High shelf 10 kHz +1.5 dB: younger, less experienced listeners prefer more bass and more treble [Olive 2015].
preset.classical.name: Classical / Orchestral
preset.classical.desc: Mild loudness compensation: classical music has a wide dynamic range and quiet passages sit 10 dB or more below the reference level, where bass is lost.
preset.classical.why: ISO 226:2003 compensation from 80 to 70 phon (listening 10 dB below the reference): low shelf 120 Hz +5.5 dB Q 0.4 and high shelf 10 kHz +1.5 dB Q 1, maximum error 0.4 dB against the curve computed from the standard.
preset.jazz.name: Jazz / Acoustic
preset.jazz.desc: Harman target with a little less bass: a drier tone for acoustic instruments and small ensembles.
preset.jazz.why: low shelf 105 Hz -2 dB: the cautious end of the 'less bass' preference (2-3 dB) [Olive 2019]. Only one tweak: no study justifies more.
preset.rock.name: Rock / Metal
preset.rock.desc: More body from kick and bass, 3 kHz presence slightly softened to cope with compressed masters and distorted guitars at high volume.
preset.rock.why: low shelf 105 Hz +4 dB: 'more bass' preference (4-6 dB) [Olive 2019]. PK 3 kHz -1.5 dB Q 1.4: 3-4 kHz is the region of the ear's highest sensitivity [ISO 226] and where the energy of distorted guitars concentrates, the first to cause fatigue.
preset.edm.name: Electronic / Hip-hop
preset.edm.desc: Sub-bass (30-60 Hz) emphasised for 808s and synth bass, voice and mids unchanged.
preset.edm.why: low shelf 60 Hz +6 dB: the high end of the 'more bass' preference (4-6 dB) [Olive 2019], moved to 60 Hz because in these genres the energy is below 60 Hz; above 150 Hz the tweak is under 0.5 dB.
preset.bass.name: Bass boost
preset.bass.desc: Harman target with 6 dB more bass.
preset.bass.why: low shelf 105 Hz +6 dB: the high end of the 'more bass' preference (4-6 dB) [Olive 2019], with the same shelf shape as the Harman target.
preset.loudness.name: Low-volume listening
preset.loudness.desc: Loudness compensation (Fletcher-Munson) for listening about 20 dB below the reference level: at low volume the ear loses bass and extreme treble. At high volume it sounds bloated.
preset.loudness.why: ISO 226:2003 compensation from 80 to 60 phon: low shelf 120 Hz +11 dB Q 0.4 and high shelf 10 kHz +3.5 dB Q 1, maximum error 0.7 dB against the curve computed from the standard.
preset.voice.name: Voice / Podcast
preset.voice.desc: Less boom from close-up microphones, voice up front, sibilance tamed.
preset.voice.why: low shelf 105 Hz -4 dB: reduces the proximity effect of podcast microphones. PK 2 kHz +2.5 dB Q 0.7: 1-4 kHz band, 72% of intelligibility [ANSI S3.5 SII]. PK 6.5 kHz -1.5 dB Q 2: the sibilance region, the same one treated by de-essers.
preset.calls.name: Calls / Meetings
preset.calls.desc: Voice up front, no boom and less hiss above the telephone band.
preset.calls.why: low shelf 105 Hz -6 dB: removes all of the Harman target's bass boost [Harman]; below 100 Hz a call contains only noise and microphone bumps. PK 2 kHz +3 dB Q 0.7: 72% of intelligibility [ANSI S3.5 SII]. High shelf 8 kHz -3 dB: wideband voice (ITU-T G.722, Bluetooth mSBC) ends at 7-8 kHz; above that only hiss and codec artefacts remain.
